1	# Agent Note: The read barrier as filesystem and process authority
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-read-barrier.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A certificate proves only what the implementer could not reach, and nothing in the repository decides that. [`dsh-verification`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) commits a `verification/certificate` only for a fully passing run and stamps it with a `CertificateIsolation` of `none`, `process`, or `host`, but its own Known Limitations name the missing read barrier: the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer of the log, and denying implementer reads is filesystem-policy work in a plugin that does not exist. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) states the requirement as principle P4, the read barrier as filesystem and process authority rather than a promise; this note is its design.
10	
11	The implementer and the checks share one filesystem and one operating-system user. `EnvironmentRunner.run()` creates the implementer's agent with `meta.cwd = workspace` and then executes every check through `ctx.shell` with `workdir: workspace` from the same process ([`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts)); its README states that the read barrier is the deployment's. The standard is in the implementer's own session log, which [`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`](../../../../packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/README.md) keeps as ordinary files under its configured root. [`dsh-credentials-local`](../../../../packages/credentials/credentials-local/README.md) already records what that costs: owner-only modes stop other operating-system users and not the model, because tool processes run as the same user and the shipped file policy confines mutations rather than reads.
12	
13	Composition decides what an implementer can read, and no composition is checked. A preset that mounts [`dsh-tool-session-query`](../../../../packages/session-query/tool-session-query/README.md) hands the model five tools that read the durable session log; one that mounts [`dsh-tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) lets it define and mount a plugin into the live process. `tools.restrict()` and subagent `toolFilter` are visibility composition per [agent-scope-contexts](../../implemented/architecture/2026-07-08-agent-scope-contexts.md), not authority, and a certificate carries no durable record of which tools its session composed.
14	
15	An isolation claim above `none` therefore has no evidence behind it. `recordRun()` writes the level its caller passes; the invariant companion validates revisions, append-only check growth, and certificate coverage, and never asks what the level asserts. Keeping only `process` and `host` runs — the reward-gaming mitigation the [trajectory-export note](2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) names, and the column the [fleet leaderboard](../../../../packages/improvement/fleet/README.md) refuses to average across — filters on an unchecked field.
16	
17	Nothing detects a workspace the implementer edited underneath its own checks. A task whose fixture supplies the tests it will be graded on is graded on whatever those files say at validation time, and the runner compares nothing between the overlay it wrote and the tree it measures.
18	
19	## Proposal
20	
21	Make the barrier authority at the executor: one policy owner, per-capability denial where each capability opens paths, and a certificate that may claim only what the composition recorded.
22	
23	**A validator-owned root.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier` (`ctx.readBarrier`) at `packages/verification/read-barrier/`: the policy home for denied reads, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../../../packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. Its `root` config defaults to `dshHomePath('verification')` through [`dsh-home-paths`](../../../../packages/util/home-paths/README.md) and accepts any absolute or `~`-prefixed directory; the service creates it owner-only (`0700`) at construction and fails loud when it exists with wider modes. `reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` for one run and returns its absolute path; the environment runner calls it before appending the `environment/run` stamp and writes there the standard snapshot, one script per check at `checks/<checkId>`, and any fixture the environment marks held out, then resolves each check's `run` against that directory so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. `protect(path)` registers one more denied directory and returns its disposer, so `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` contributes its session-store root as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration; `denyRoots` remains a config field for directories no plugin owns. `resolve({ session? })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied, enforcement }`, and `denies(policy, target)` decides containment.
24	
25	| Field | Meaning |
26	|---|---|
27	| `root` (default `dshHomePath('verification')`) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed directory the barrier owns; created `0700`, rejected when it already exists with wider modes. |
28	| `denyRoots` (default `[]`) | Additional absolute directories denied alongside `root`, for directories no plugin registers through `protect()`. |
29	| `hostAttestation` (optional absolute path) | File an external account writes; without a verified one the barrier refuses a `host` claim. |
30	
31	The denied set for a role is not among them: which authorities an `implementer` may hold is a security invariant, not a deployment choice.
32	
33	**The deny rule.** For a session whose role is `implementer`, a read is denied when the target's canonical path is a denied directory or a descendant of one. Containment is decided the way [`dsh-fs-sandbox`](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-14-cross-family-fs-sandbox.md) decides it: canonicalize first, then test identity or descent through `ctx.fs.contains(parent, child)` on resolved targets, so the policy parses no path strings and an ancestor symlink swapped since resolution is caught by re-canonicalizing immediately before the decision. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing; `unrestricted` is the default and leaves every shipped preset exactly as it is today.
34	
35	**The fs policy plugin.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier` at `packages/fs/fs-read-barrier/`, the read counterpart of the write and edit policy [`dsh-fs-observation-policy`](../../../../packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/README.md) contributes through the same event gate. It registers no service and declares no `Config`, because every deployment-varying value belongs to the barrier above: it injects `readBarrier` and decides one new event. [`dsh-fs`](../../../../packages/fs/fs/README.md) declares `fs/read-intent(target, actor, next)` beside `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent`, as a `@mode waterfall` returning `FsReadDenial { code: FsErrorCode; message: string } | undefined`; unlike the two single-slot intents this one delegates, because a barrier that owned the slot would stop every later read policy from deciding. The plugin returns a denial for a contained target and calls `next()` otherwise. `FsErrorCode` gains `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`. `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches the event inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before `ctx.fs.stat`, so a denied path never reveals presence or absence, and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` dispatches it on the `view` command. The tool layer adds no recovery instruction, because no retry of the same call succeeds; the model sees the policy's message verbatim.
36	
37	##### Exact error
38	
39	```markdown
40	read denied: "<path>" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it
41	```
42	
43	**What a denial records.** The barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/denied` session event per refusal, carrying `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, where `capability` names the seam that refused (`fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`). The path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the event adds evidence and no new disclosure. It is a `SessionEventMap` member with `ignorable: true`, so a build that does not know the type still reads the log under the [version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md).
44	
45	**Tool authority and the composition-time guard.** `ToolDefinition` in [`dsh-tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) gains `authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]`, never model-visible, where `ToolAuthority` is a merge-extensible union declared by `dsh-tools` with three members at the start: `session-log` (the tool reads durable session events), `plugin-mount` (it mounts or evaluates code in the live runtime), and `runtime-introspection` (it reports the live composition). `dsh-tool-session-query` declares `session-log` on all five of its tools; `dsh-tool-cordis` declares `plugin-mount` on `cordis_define`, `cordis_run`, `cordis_stop`, and `cordis_undefine`, and `runtime-introspection` on `cordis_inspect`. An `implementer` session may compose none of the three. Declaring authority at the tool, rather than a name list at the barrier, means a tool added later is covered by its own declaration.
46	
47	**How a preset declares its role.** A preset's optional `preset.yml` gains `role: implementer | validator | unrestricted`, absent meaning `unrestricted`. It is the one authority claim that file carries, so [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../../../packages/preset/agent-presets/README.md) refuses `validator` from a `user`-trust preset and lists that preset as `broken` with the reason: a locally authored preset that could name itself `validator` would grant itself reads. This is the roster's first enforcing use of `trust`, and its README changes with it. `mountPreset` audits the role after `handle.await()` settles the subtree, beside `inactiveRows`, and rejects the mount when the declared role is `implementer` and any tool in the preset's scope layer declares a denied authority. Because the audit runs inside the agent factory's `setup`, a rejected composition rolls the whole session creation back, so the failure is loud and nothing half-composed survives.
48	
49	##### Exact mount refusal
50	
51	```markdown
52	agent-presets: preset "<id>" declares role "implementer" but composes "<tool>", which carries the "<authority>" authority
53	```
54	
55	**The runtime guard.** The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` through the agent's own context at session setup, denying any execution whose definition carries a denied authority for that session's role. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission ([`ToolGuard`](../../../../packages/core/tools/src/index.ts)). The mount audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards, including one a subagent driver contributes.
56	
57	##### Exact guard denial
58	
59	```markdown
60	"<tool>" carries the "<authority>" authority and is not callable in an implementer session
61	```
62	
63	**Process-level denial.** The [sandbox seam](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-06-sandbox.md) expresses file effects only, which is why a confined subprocess can still read anything it reaches. `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy` gain `deniedReadRoots: readonly string[]`; `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()` fills it from `ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })`, so the fs fence and every process runner keep taking one owner-resolved policy per call. `dsh-sandbox-local` implements it per backend — a `bwrap` `--tmpfs` over each root, a Landlock ruleset that omits read access for them, a Seatbelt `(deny file-read* (subpath …))` clause, and the Windows ACL runner's equivalent deny entry — and reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` when the selected backend cannot express the denial, so the claim fails rather than the barrier. [`dsh-bash-sandbox`](../../../../packages/shell/bash-sandbox/README.md), `dsh-pwsh-sandbox`, and [`dsh-terminal-bash`](../../../../packages/terminal/terminal-bash/README.md) inherit it without changes. [`dsh-tool-fs-search`](../../../../packages/fs/tool-fs-search/README.md) spawns ripgrep unconfined through `ctx.subprocess` today; it confines that spawn through `ctx.sandbox.confine()` whenever a barrier is in force, and additionally the barrier's tool guard denies a `glob` or `grep` whose `path` argument names a denied root directly.
64	
65	**Executors the barrier cannot confine.** Two composed capabilities open paths the harness cannot fence in-process. [`dsh-workflow-worker-thread`](../../../../packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/README.md) states that its worker is not a security sandbox and that an escaped script recovers Node capabilities with the host process's privileges. The out-of-process [subagent](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) providers — `subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk` — launch a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness policy. For an `implementer` session, both refuse to start under a claim of `process` or `host` and record `unenforced` under a claim of `none`. The in-process subagent drivers need no exception: a child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, so it inherits the same census, the same scope layer, and the same role.
66	
67	**The scope census.** Before the session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` event carrying `{ version, role, presetId, root, denied, census, enforcement }`. `census` is one entry per tool visible to the agent, `{ name, authority }`, which makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only; the invariant cross-checks it against the tool names in each `request/header`'s assembled schemas, so a tool added after the census is caught. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability the composition registered — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, `workflow` — valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`.
68	
69	**The certificate invariant.** `recordRun()` reads `ctx.get('readBarrier')` and refuses to commit a certificate whose isolation exceeds what the session recorded, with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`; the [`./invariant`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) companion applies the identical rule to the durable stream, so a forged certificate fails replay wherever the companion is installed. Independently of level, both refuse a certificate on a session whose scope census carries a denied authority: composing a log-reading tool forfeits the certificate even when the guard was somehow bypassed. `CertificateIsolation`'s JSDoc changes with the rule: `process` means what the ladder below states rather than in-process read policy alone.
70	
71	**The `host` marker.** `host` is accepted only from a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier wrote after verifying a file at the configured `hostAttestation` path: it must exist, be owned by a uid other than the harness process's effective uid, be unwritable by that uid and its groups, and contain exactly the run's environment content hashes as the `environment/run` stamp carries them. An in-process component cannot produce that file without already holding another account's privileges, which is the property the level asserts. On Windows the ownership and write tests read the ACL through the primitives `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl` already owns. Absent or unverifiable, the barrier records no attestation and the claim is refused.
72	
73	**Tamper on check-owned paths.** Check-owned paths are the barrier's denied directories plus the workspace paths an environment declares immutable: `EnvironmentDefinition.task` gains `immutable?: readonly string[]`, workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script. The runner already hashes a directory in `hashDirectory`; it records the digest of the check-owned set immediately after the fixture overlay and before the implementer's first turn, and again at each validation. The `verification/run` event that the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) adds carries the attempt's `treeHash`; this note adds `verdict: 'pass' | 'fail' | 'tampered'`. A digest that differs from the baseline is `tampered`: the runner records the run, issues one directive naming tamper without naming a path, stops the attempt loop because the workspace no longer measures the task, and never calls `recordRun`, so no certificate can exist for that run. `foldTrajectory` gains reward basis `tamper` with `outcome: 0`, which outranks any certificate in the same log, and the invariant companion rejects a certificate that follows a `tampered` run.
74	
75	**A blind judge under one licence.** Cross-provider routing is the first answer to a judge whose label affects it, and a deployment with one model licence cannot take it. The second route is filesystem and process isolation plus a judge session that holds no implementer context, which means all of the following and nothing weaker. The judge session is created through `ctx.agents.create` with a fresh `SessionId`, no `parentSessionId`, and no resume or fork seed, so its log begins at its own creation. Its `meta.cwd` is a judge workspace holding a copy of the implementer's tree at the audited attempt's `treeHash`, never the implementer's workspace. Its derived history contains exactly the judge preset's system prompt, the environment's task prompt, and one user message carrying the evidence the auditor chose; no `assistant/message`, `tool/result`, or `verification/directive` from the audited session reaches it. Its preset is `system`-trust and declares `role: validator`, so the composition-time guard still denies it a log-reading tool: a judge that could read the audited log would reconstruct the implementer's reasoning and lose the independence this arrangement provides. The barrier appends a `judge/session` event naming the audited session id and asserting the empty lineage, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session whose header carries a parent or a seed.
76	
77	## The isolation ladder
78	
79	| Level | What it asserts | Required enforcement | Durable evidence |
80	|---|---|---|---|
81	| `none` | Nothing. Implementer and validator share a filesystem. | None. | The certificate alone; a scope event when the barrier is composed. |
82	| `process` | No executor of the implementer's session opens a denied path. | Every composed path-opening capability records `denied-at-executor`; the session's sandbox mode is `workspace-write` or narrower; workflow workers and out-of-process subagent providers refuse to start. | A `read-barrier/scope` event before the first `request/header`, with role `implementer`, an empty denied-authority intersection, and no `unenforced` entry. |
83	| `host` | The checks and fixtures are outside the harness account's write reach. | Everything `process` requires. | Everything `process` requires plus a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier verified from a file the harness process cannot write. |
84	
85	## Alternatives considered
86	
87	**Omit the tools and trust the prompt.** Schema omission and instruction are not enforcement when another caller reaches the same operation, which is why the packages standard requires the decision in the operation that makes it. The barrier denies at the executor and the acceptance criteria test denial there.
88	
89	**Deny reads through `SandboxMode` instead of a separate policy.** `SandboxMode` is a three-value file-effect vocabulary shared by every enforcing family; a fourth value meaning "and cannot read these paths" would make one enum carry two independent decisions, and every consumer that switches on the mode would have to learn the second. `deniedReadRoots` rides the same per-call policy without changing what a mode means.
90	
91	**Subclass the filesystem provider the way `fs-sandbox` does.** One provider registers `ctx.fs` per context and `SandboxedFileSystem` already extends `LocalFileSystem`, so a second fence by inheritance would force a mixin or a fixed provider ladder. The `fs/*` event gate is the layer built for adding policy without a service dependency, and it degrades to the bare provider when the plugin is absent.
92	
93	**Name the forbidden tools in the barrier's config.** A name list is stale the moment a package adds a log-reading tool, and a deployment could shorten it. Authority declared at the tool is carried by the tool, and the denied set for a role is a security invariant rather than a tunable.
94	
95	**Derive the role from the session creator instead of the preset.** The creator knows the intent; only the composition knows what was actually mounted, and the failure this prevents is a preset that composes a tool its role forbids. The preset declares the role, the mount audit checks the composition against it, and the creator's request is refused when the resolved preset's role does not match.
96	
97	**Infer `host` from configuration.** The environment runner already rejected inferred isolation for the same reason: nothing in-process can observe the deployment's arrangement, so an inferred value either devalues an isolated run or lies about a local one. A file another account owns is the smallest fact that cannot be produced from inside the process.
98	
99	**Score tamper as a failing check.** A failed check means the work is incomplete; a modified test means the measurement is void. Folding them would let a trajectory earn partial credit for a workspace whose checks no longer describe the task, so tamper is its own verdict and its own reward basis.
100	
101	**Give the judge the implementer's transcript for context.** A judge that reads the audited reasoning inherits its framing, and the same-lineage mislabeling the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) records is what the blind session exists to avoid. The judge receives the task, the tree, and the evidence the auditor selected.
102	
103	## Acceptance criteria
104	
105	- In a Loader-booted composition over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier/`, a `read` of a file under the barrier root from an `implementer`-role session fails with `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED` and the exact message above, one `read-barrier/denied` event is appended, and the same call from a `validator`-role session in the same process returns the file's content.
106	- The denial is proved through the executor, not the schema: the implementer's `read` tool is registered and visible, and a direct `ctx.fs.readText` from a trusted plugin still succeeds, which the test asserts so the threat model stays explicit.
107	- Mounting the preset at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-guard/`, which declares `role: implementer` and composes `dsh-tool-session-query`, rejects with the exact mount refusal and leaves no session behind; a `user`-trust preset declaring `role: validator` is listed `broken` with its reason; and the invariant companion rejects a certificate on a hand-authored log whose scope census carries the `session-log` authority.
108	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'host'` on a session with no verified attestation refuses with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN` and commits no certificate; the invariant companion rejects a hand-authored log carrying that certificate at the certificate record.
109	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'process'` on a session whose scope event records any `unenforced` capability refuses the same way, and succeeds once every composed capability records `denied-at-executor`.
110	- Over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-tamper/`, whose environment marks its test file immutable and whose scripted model overwrites it, the attempt's `verification/run` carries `verdict: 'tampered'`, no certificate exists, the goal stays out of `complete`, and the exported trajectory line has `outcome: 0` with basis `tamper`.
111	- A judge session created for an audited session has no `parentSessionId` and no seed, its derived history holds exactly the judge system prompt, the task prompt, and the evidence message, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session that carries either.
112	- Two keyless snapshots record what the model sees: `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-denied/` pins the denial text in the transcript and the session log, and `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-tamper/` pins the tamper directive's `<validation_failed>` follow-up. Both replay on macOS and Linux per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
113	
114	## Rollout
115	
116	Each slice lands with its own tests and leaves the gates green on its own.
117	
118	1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier` with the root, `reserve`, `protect`, `resolve`, `denies`, the `read-barrier/scope` and `read-barrier/denied` events, and its invariant companion. Enforcement records `unenforced` everywhere; nothing is denied yet, and no existing composition changes behavior.
119	2. `fs/read-intent` in `dsh-fs`, `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`, the dispatches in `dsh-tool-fs` and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier`. Adds the `read-barrier` fixture and the `read-barrier-denied` snapshot.
120	3. `ToolAuthority` on `ToolDefinition`, the declarations in `dsh-tool-session-query` and `dsh-tool-cordis`, `role` in `preset.yml`, the `mountPreset` audit, and the per-agent tool guard. Adds the `read-barrier-guard` fixture.
121	4. The certificate invariant: the `recordRun` precondition, the companion's rule, the `read-barrier/attestation` event and its file check, and the `CertificateIsolation` documentation change. The environment runner gains `EnvironmentRunRequest.preset` and refuses a claim above `none` when the resolved preset's role is not `implementer`.
122	5. `deniedReadRoots` on `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy`, the `dsh-sandbox-local` backends, the `dsh-sandbox-policy` fill from the barrier, the confined ripgrep spawn in `dsh-tool-fs-search`, and the refusals in the workflow engine and the out-of-process subagent providers. This is the slice that makes `process` claimable.
123	6. Tamper: `task.immutable` in `dsh-environments`, the runner's baseline and per-attempt digest over check-owned paths, `verdict` on `verification/run`, the `tamper` reward basis in `dsh-trajectories`, and the `read-barrier-tamper` fixture and snapshot. It follows the `verification/run` event from the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md).
124	7. The blind judge: the shipped `system`-trust judge preset, the lineage-free creation path, the `judge/session` event, and the invariant that rejects a seeded judge. The judging Consumer itself belongs to the oversight seam of the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md).
125	
126	## Risks
127	
128	The barrier is trusted code in the implementer's own process below `host`. A plugin with direct `Session` or `ctx.fs` access appends counterfeit events and reads any path, exactly as `dsh-verification` already states for its durable records. The ladder is honest about this: `none` claims nothing, `process` claims only that the composed executors deny, and `host` is the only level whose evidence comes from outside the process.
129	
130	`process` costs enforcement a deployment may not want. Confining every ripgrep spawn, refusing workflow workers, and refusing out-of-process subagent providers removes capability from implementer sessions that claim it; a deployment that wants those capabilities runs at `none` and keeps a certificate that says so.
131	
132	A check's command line stays observable. The barrier protects the script's content and the fixtures, not the argv a process listing shows, so an environment whose check name or arguments encode the assertion leaks it. Environment authors keep the assertion in the script.
133	
134	The census is only as complete as the composition it was taken from. It is appended before the first request and cross-checked against each `request/header`'s tool names, which catches a tool added later but not a plugin that reads paths without registering a tool at all.
135	
136	Tamper detection is a digest comparison, so it reports that the check-owned set changed and never who changed it or how. 138	Making `trust` enforcing for one field changes what the roster promises. A deployment that configured a `user` root expecting presets to be ordinary compositions now finds one class of declaration refused there; the refusal is listed as a `broken` reason on the same roster page that offers to delete it.

Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

</system-reminder>

2	 * The sandbox POLICY home (`ctx.sandboxPolicy`): the single owner of the
3	 * deployment's sandbox fallbacks plus per-session resolution: the file-effect
4	 * {@link SandboxMode}, the `workspace-write` root, and the override kit (the
5	 * `sandbox/mode` event, its fold, and its write path, from `./session-mode.ts`).
6	 * Before each agent request, the owner also contributes the resolved policy to
7	 * the cache-safe runtime-context snapshot. The agent loop logs that snapshot as
8	 * model history, so replay reconstructs the same mode and root the enforcing
9	 * consumers resolve without rewriting the stable system prompt.
10	 *
11	 * Enforcing filesystem, one-shot bash, and terminal backends read the SAME
12	 * resolved policy here. The context describes that policy without inventorying
13	 * capabilities, while each backend retains its own enforcement dialect and each
14	 * tool owns its operation-specific denial and escalation guidance. The service
15	 * reads session state once at each operation boundary; executors and providers
16	 * remain session-free.

39	  switch (policy.mode) {
40	    case 'read-only':
41	      return 'Current DSH file policy: read-only. Any available operation enforced by the DSH file sandbox cannot modify files in the standing mode. Do not refuse a required modification from this policy alone: try an available tool normally and follow any denial and escalation guidance it returns.'
42	    case 'workspace-write':

70	  /**

85	/**

87	 * default mode, fallback workspace root, and current request-time policy
88	 * section. Tool layers call {@link resolve} for each execution so a session's
89	 * mode log and immutable cwd travel together to every enforcing capability.
90	 */
91	export class SandboxPolicyService extends Service {
92	  // Inline schema call: the config catalog walks `static Config` statically.
93	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
94	    mode: z.union(['read-only', 'workspace-write', 'danger-full-access'] as const).default('read-only'),
95	    // No schema default: process.cwd() is resolved in the constructor so the
96	    // stored root is always absolute regardless of how it was supplied.
97	    workspaceRoot: z.string(),
98	  })

100	  /** The deployment default mode — the fallback beneath a session override. */
101	  readonly defaultMode: SandboxMode
102	  /** The absolute `workspace-write` fallback root for calls without a session cwd. */
103	  readonly workspaceRoot: string
104	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {

107	    // runtime fact. `workspaceRoot` has NO schema default, so its fallback to
108	    // the process cwd is real branching, resolved absolute either way.
109	    this.defaultMode = config.mode as SandboxMode
110	    this.workspaceRoot = resolveWorkspaceRoot(config.workspaceRoot ?? process.cwd())

112	    ctx.inject(['systemPrompt'], (scope: Context) => {
113	      scope.systemPrompt.context({
114	        name: 'sandbox:policy',
115	        order: 110,
116	        text: (context) => {
117	          const session = context.agent?.session

126	  /**

128	   * mode outranks the session's last `sandbox/mode` event, which outranks the
129	   * deployment default. A session cwd is its workspace-write boundary; the
130	   * configured root is the fallback for agentless calls and sessions without a
131	   * cwd.
132	   * @param request - optional session and approved mode override.
133	   * @returns the fully resolved per-call mode and absolute workspace root.
134	   */
135	  resolve(request: SandboxPolicyRequest = {}): SandboxExecutionPolicy {
136	    const { session } = request
137	    return {
138	      mode: request.mode ?? (session === undefined ? undefined : this.overrideOf(session)) ?? this.defaultMode,
139	      workspaceRoot: resolveWorkspaceRoot(session?.header.cwd ?? this.workspaceRoot),
140	      ...session === undefined ? {} : { sessionId: session.id },
141	    }
142	  }
143	
144	  /**
145	   * Read the session override without applying the deployment default.
146	   * @param session - session whose log supplies the override.
147	   * @returns the last logged mode, or `undefined` without one.
148	   */
149	  overrideOf(session: Session): SandboxMode | undefined {
150	    return effectiveSandboxMode(session.events)
151	  }
152	}

2	 * Vocabulary for the filesystem Service Definition (`ctx.fs`): the opaque target/version
3	 * identities, the metadata `stat` returns, the write-intent and outcome shapes, the
4	 * literal-edit request/outcome, and the typed error taxonomy.

8	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'

11	/**
12	 * Opaque key for stale guards and target lookup. The local backend uses a
13	 * realpath-like string; a remote backend might use a workspace URI or file id.
14	 * Consumers MUST NOT parse it or assume it is a local absolute path.
15	 */
16	export type FsTargetKey = Branded<'FsTargetKey'>

18	/**
19	 * Brand a string as an {@link FsTargetKey}. For backend use only — a consumer
20	 * never manufactures a key, it receives one from `resolve()`.
21	 * @param key - the backend's raw key string (the local backend passes a realpath).
22	 * @returns the same string, branded; no validation is performed.
23	 */
24	export function FsTargetKey(key: string): FsTargetKey {
25	  return key as FsTargetKey
26	}
27	
28	/**
29	 * Opaque file-version token — the freshness token a write/edit guards against.
30	 * The local backend derives it from high-resolution stat identity and freshness
31	 * fields; a remote backend might use a revision id. The policy layer records it
32	 * for stale checks; consumers may display related metadata but MUST NOT
33	 * interpret this token.
34	 */
35	export type FsVersion = Branded<'FsVersion'>
36	
37	/**
38	 * Brand a string as an {@link FsVersion}. For backend use only — a consumer
39	 * never manufactures a version, it receives one from `stat`/write/edit outcomes.
40	 * @param v - the backend's raw version string.
41	 * @returns the same string, branded; no validation is performed.
42	 */
43	export function FsVersion(v: string): FsVersion {
44	  return v as FsVersion
45	}
46	
47	/**
48	 * One authoritative observation of a target. A present observation carries the
49	 * version used by guarded replacement; an absent observation authorizes only a
50	 * guarded create, never an edit.
51	 */
52	export type FsObservation =
53	  | { readonly kind: 'present'; readonly version: FsVersion }
54	  | { readonly kind: 'absent' }
55	
56	/**
57	 * A path resolved by a backend into a stable identity. `resolve()` produces
58	 * this; every other operation takes it.
59	 */
60	export interface FsTarget {
61	  /** Opaque key for stale guards and target lookup. */
62	  targetKey: FsTargetKey
63	  /**
64	   * Path for model/UI-facing output. May be a local absolute path,
65	   * workspace-relative path, or remote URI depending on the backend.
66	   */
67	  displayPath: string
68	}

70	/**
71	 * Metadata about a target — what {@link FileSystem.stat} returns. Lets the
72	 * policy layer reject directories/special files before reading and choose
73	 * `readText` vs `streamText` from `size` without probing by failure. `version`
74	 * is the freshness token. `undefined` from `stat` means the target is absent.
75	 */
76	export interface FsInfo {
77	  /** Opaque freshness token of the target right now. */
78	  version: FsVersion
79	  /** Whether the target is a regular file, a directory, or something else. */
80	  type: 'file' | 'directory' | 'other'
81	  /** Byte size of a regular file, when the backend can report it. */
82	  size?: number

84	
85	/**
86	 * Metadata about a path without following the final path component when it is a
87	 * symbolic link. Unlike {@link FsInfo}, this path-level probe can report
88	 * `symlink` so consumers with trust-boundary rules can reject repository-owned
89	 * links before resolving a target.
90	 */
91	export interface FsPathInfo {
92	  /** Opaque freshness token of the path entry right now. */
93	  version: FsVersion
94	  /** Whether the path entry is a regular file, directory, symlink, or other. */
95	  type: 'file' | 'directory' | 'symlink' | 'other'
96	  /** Byte size of the path entry, when the backend can report it. */
97	  size?: number
98	}

100	/**
101	 * One direct child returned by {@link FileSystem.listDir}. Listing returns
102	 * metadata and resolved targets only; it must not read file contents.
103	 */
104	export interface FsDirEntry {
105	  /** Basename of the child inside the listed directory. */
106	  name: string
107	  /** Whether the child is a regular file, a directory, or something else. */
108	  type: 'file' | 'directory' | 'other'
109	  /** Resolved child target for follow-up operations. */
110	  target: FsTarget
111	  /** Opaque freshness token when the backend can report metadata cheaply. */
112	  version?: FsVersion
113	  /** Byte size of a regular file, when the backend can report it. */
114	  size?: number
115	}

117	/**
118	 * Guarded write intent. `createIfAbsent` rejects an existing target with
119	 * `FS_NOT_OBSERVED`; `replaceIfVersion` rejects absence or mismatch with
120	 * `FS_STALE_VERSION`. Omitting the intent from `writeText` means unconditional
121	 * create-or-overwrite, not a third union arm.
122	 */
123	export type FsWriteIntent =
124	  | { kind: 'createIfAbsent' }
125	  | { kind: 'replaceIfVersion'; version: FsVersion }
126	
127	/** Outcome of a full-file write. */
128	export interface FsWriteOutcome {
129	  /** Whether the write created a new file or replaced an existing one. */
130	  operation: 'create' | 'update'
131	  /** Opaque version of the file after the write. */
132	  version: FsVersion
133	  /**
134	   * The file's content BEFORE the write, or `null` when the file did not exist
135	   * (a create) or the backend declined a contextual basis (for example, a
136	   * binary/non-UTF-8 prior file or either overwrite side reaching its exclusive limit).
137	   * LF-normalized storage text (the diff basis), never a diff — a consumer
138	   * computes the result-time contextual diff from `before`/`after` when
139	   * `before` is present, else falls back to a whole-file diff.
140	   */
141	  before: string | null
142	  /** The file's content AFTER the write, LF-normalized to share `before`'s diff basis. */
143	  after: string
144	}
145	
146	/** A literal-replacement edit request. */
147	export interface FsEditRequest {
148	  /** Literal non-empty text to replace. Must match exactly (after line-ending normalization). */
149	  oldString: string
150	  /** Literal replacement text. An empty string deletes the matched text. */
151	  newString: string
152	  /** Replace every match instead of requiring exactly one. */
153	  replaceAll: boolean
154	}
155	
156	/** Outcome of a literal edit. */
157	export interface FsEditOutcome {
158	  /** Opaque version of the file after the edit. */
159	  version: FsVersion
160	  /**
161	   * The file's content BEFORE the edit. Raw storage text (LF-normalized by the
162	   * backend), never a diff — a consumer computes the result-time contextual diff
163	   * (the applied hunk with context) from `before`/`after`.
164	   */
165	  before: string
166	  /** The file's content AFTER the edit. */
167	  after: string
168	}
169	
170	/**
171	 * Stable, machine-routable codes for filesystem failures. Carried on
172	 * {@link FsError}; the tool registry exposes `{ name, code }` on `isError`
173	 * results so retry/permission/UI layers can branch without parsing messages.
174	 */
175	export type FsErrorCode =
176	  | 'FS_NOT_FOUND'
177	  | 'FS_NOT_DIRECTORY'
178	  | 'FS_NOT_TEXT'
179	  | 'FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE'
180	  | 'FS_TOO_LARGE'
181	  | 'FS_PERMISSION_DENIED'
182	  | 'FS_SANDBOX_DENIED'
183	  | 'FS_IO_ERROR'
184	  | 'FS_STALE_VERSION'
185	  | 'FS_NOT_OBSERVED'
186	  | 'FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT'
187	  | 'FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND'
188	  | 'FS_ABORTED'
189	
190	/**
191	 * Typed filesystem error. Extends {@link HarnessError} so it carries a stable
192	 * {@link FsErrorCode} and chains `cause`. `dsh-fs` owns this vocabulary so
193	 * backends and the policy layer raise the same codes instead of each inventing
194	 * message strings.
195	 */
196	export class FsError extends HarnessError {
197	  override readonly code: FsErrorCode
198	
199	  constructor(message: string, code: FsErrorCode, options?: ErrorOptions) {
200	    super(message, code, options)
201	    this.code = code
202	  }
203	}

1	/**
2	 * Event-only filesystem observation policy; it registers no service. A weak owner/target map
3	 * records every authoritative presence/absence observation, single-slot intent listeners derive
4	 * guards from that state, and the provider performs the atomic freshness/no-clobber check. Without
5	 * this plugin, tools retain the bare provider's unconditional mutation behavior. See the package
6	 * README for composition rules.
7	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-policy
8	 */
9	
10	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
11	import { FsError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs'
12	import type { FsObservation, FsTarget, FsVersion, FsWriteIntent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs'
13	import type { FsObservationActor } from './types.ts'
14	
15	export type { FsObservationActor } from './types.ts'
16	
17	/**
18	 * Per-context observed-file state and the three `fs/*` decisions over it. One
19	 * instance is created per `apply()` so disposal can drop all state for HMR.
20	 */
21	class ObservedStateGate {
22	  /**
23	   * Observed-file state, keyed first by the owner object (weakly held, so a
24	   * collected session frees its state), then by {@link FsTarget.targetKey}. An
25	   * entry's presence is the prior-observation record; its discriminant keeps
26	   * confirmed absence distinct from an unseen target.
27	   */
28	  private observed = new WeakMap<object, Map<string, FsObservation>>()
29	
30	  /**
31	   * Derive the observed-state owner from the opaque event actor — normally the
32	   * active agent session. `undefined` when no owner can be derived (e.g. a
33	   * direct tool call with no agent); such calls read freely but cannot satisfy
34	   * the write/edit prior-observation policy.
35	   */
36	  private owner(actor: object | undefined): object | undefined {
37	    // tsgolint treats object as assignable to weak FsObservationActor, while tsc still requires the structural cast for property access.
38	    // See the analyzer-divergence consequence in .agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-29-oxlint-linter.md.
39	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion -- The analyzers disagree on this weak type.
40	    return (actor as FsObservationActor | undefined)?.agent?.session
41	  }
42	
43	  private get(owner: object, targetKey: string): FsObservation | undefined {
44	    return this.observed.get(owner)?.get(targetKey)
45	  }
46	
47	  private set(owner: object, targetKey: string, observation: FsObservation): void {
48	    let byTarget = this.observed.get(owner)
49	    if (!byTarget) {
50	      byTarget = new Map()
51	      this.observed.set(owner, byTarget)
52	    }
53	    byTarget.set(targetKey, observation)
54	  }
55	
56	  /** Drop all recorded state (HMR safety / disposal). */
57	  clear(): void {
58	    this.observed = new WeakMap()
59	  }
60	
61	  /**
62	   * Decide the write intent: unseen or confirmed absent ⇒ `createIfAbsent`;
63	   * confirmed present ⇒ `replaceIfVersion` at the observed version.
64	   */
65	  writeIntent(target: FsTarget, actor: object | undefined): FsWriteIntent {
66	    const owner = this.owner(actor)
67	    const prior = owner ? this.get(owner, target.targetKey) : undefined
68	    return prior?.kind === 'present'
69	      ? { kind: 'replaceIfVersion', version: prior.version }
70	      : { kind: 'createIfAbsent' }
71	  }
72	
73	  /**
74	   * Decide the edit version guard: unseen rejects with `FS_NOT_OBSERVED`,
75	   * confirmed absence rejects with `FS_NOT_FOUND`, and presence supplies the
76	   * observed version as the CAS basis.
77	   */
78	  editIntent(target: FsTarget, actor: object | undefined): { version: FsVersion } {
79	    const owner = this.owner(actor)
80	    const prior = owner ? this.get(owner, target.targetKey) : undefined
81	    if (!owner || prior === undefined) {
82	      throw new FsError(`edit requires reading "${target.displayPath}" first`, 'FS_NOT_OBSERVED')
83	    }
84	    if (prior.kind === 'absent') {
85	      throw new FsError(`cannot edit "${target.displayPath}": not found`, 'FS_NOT_FOUND')
86	    }
87	    return { version: prior.version }
88	  }
89	
90	  /** Record an authoritative present or absent observation for this owner and target. */
91	  observe(target: FsTarget, observation: FsObservation, actor: object | undefined): void {
92	    const owner = this.owner(actor)
93	    if (owner) this.set(owner, target.targetKey, observation)
94	  }
95	}
96	
97	/** Cordis plugin name used by loader diagnostics. */
98	export const name = 'fs-observation-policy'
99	
100	/**
101	 * Register the three `fs/*` listeners. No `inject` — this plugin reads no
102	 * services; it operates only on its own `WeakMap`. The waterfalls are unbound
103	 * (the tool dispatches them with no `this`), so the listeners take the raw
104	 * `(target, actor, next)` arguments.
105	 */
106	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
107	  const gate = new ObservedStateGate()
108	
109	  ctx.effect(() => () => {
110	    // Drop all recorded state on disposal so a reloaded plugin starts clean
111	    // (HMR safety). The WeakMap itself would be GC'd, but replacing it makes the
112	    // release observable and immediate for tests.
113	    gate.clear()
114	  }, 'fs-observation-policy observed-state teardown')
115	
116	  // fs/write-intent: occupy the single decision slot — do NOT call next().
117	  // Deferred through Promise.resolve().then so the declared Promise return type
118	  // holds (a throw rejects, never escapes synchronously through the waterfall).
119	  ctx.on('fs/write-intent', (target, actor) => Promise.resolve().then(() => gate.writeIntent(target, actor)))
120	
121	  // fs/edit-intent: occupy the single decision slot — do not call next().
122	  ctx.on('fs/edit-intent', (target, actor) => Promise.resolve().then(() => gate.editIntent(target, actor)))
123	
124	  // fs/observed must remain synchronous and non-throwing: emit does not await
125	  // promises, and successful mutations have already committed. WeakMap.set
126	  // satisfies that contract for both presence and absence.
127	  ctx.on('fs/observed', (target, observation, actor) => {
128	    gate.observe(target, observation, actor)
129	  })
130	}

1	/**
2	 * Model-facing UTF-8 read. It performs one provider stat for type, routing, and observed version,
3	 * streams large or size-unknown files, renders a bounded window, then emits the observation.
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs/src/read
5	 */
6	
7	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
8	import { defineTool } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
9	import type { GenericCallView, ReadResultView, ToolResult } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
10	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs'
11	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt'
12	import { buildWindow, formatReadOutput, langFromPath, readMetaFromMeta } from './read-render.ts'
13	import { resolveRegularReadTarget } from './read-target.ts'
14	
15	/** Default and maximum number of lines returned by one `read` call (the `readLimit` config). */
16	export const READ_LIMIT = 2000
17	
18	/**
19	 * Default streaming threshold (the `readStreamMinSize` config): files at or
20	 * above this size stream; smaller files read whole into memory.
21	 */
22	export const STREAM_MIN_SIZE = 10 * 1024 * 1024
23	
24	/** Resolved read-tool caps — plugin config after defaulting (see `Config` in index.ts). */
25	export interface ReadToolCaps {
26	  /** Default and maximum number of lines returned by one call. */
27	  limit: number
28	  /** Maximum characters returned for a single line. */
29	  maxLineLength: number
30	  /** Maximum bytes returned for selected file lines. */
31	  maxBytes: number
32	  /** Files at or above this size stream; smaller files read whole into memory. */
33	  streamMinSize: number
34	}
35	
36	/** Validated `read` arguments after defaulting. */
37	interface ReadInput {
38	  filePath: string
39	  offset: number
40	  limit: number
41	}
42	
43	function parsePositiveInteger(value: number, name: string): number {
44	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || !Number.isInteger(value) || value < 1) {
45	    throw new Error(`${name} must be a positive integer`)
46	  }
47	  return value
48	}
49	
50	/**
51	 * Validate value constraints the schema DSL can't express. `maxLimit` is the deployment's line cap.
52	 * @param args - the schema-validated raw tool arguments; `offset`/`limit` must be positive integers when given.
53	 * @param maxLimit - the configured line cap: both the default `limit` and the largest one accepted.
54	 * @returns the validated input with `offset` defaulted to 1 and `limit` to `maxLimit`.
55	 */
56	export function parseReadArgs(args: { file_path: string; offset?: number; limit?: number }, maxLimit: number): ReadInput {
57	  if (args.file_path.trim().length === 0) throw new Error('file_path must be a non-empty string')
58	  const offset = args.offset === undefined ? 1 : parsePositiveInteger(args.offset, 'offset')
59	  const limit = args.limit === undefined ? maxLimit : parsePositiveInteger(args.limit, 'limit')
60	  if (limit > maxLimit) throw new Error(`limit must be less than or equal to ${maxLimit}`)
61	  return { filePath: args.file_path, offset, limit }
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Register the `read` tool and its system-prompt guidance.
66	 * @param ctx - the plugin context; registrations are effects scoped to it, and execution uses its `fs` service.
67	 * @param caps - the deployment's resolved read caps (plugin config after defaulting).
68	 */
69	export function applyReadTool(ctx: Context, caps: ReadToolCaps): void {
70	  ctx.systemPrompt.section({
71	    name: 'tool:read',
72	    order: 100,
73	    text: 'Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.',
74	  })
75	
76	  ctx.tools.register(defineTool({
77	    name: 'read',
78	    description: 'Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.',
79	    parameters: {
80	      file_path: { type: 'string', required: true, description: 'Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.' },
81	      offset: { type: 'number', description: '1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.' },
82	      limit: { type: 'number', description: `Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to ${caps.limit}.` },
83	    },
84	    output: {
85	      schema: {
86	        type: 'object',
87	        additionalProperties: false,
88	        properties: {
89	          path: { type: 'string', required: true },
90	          offset: { type: 'integer', required: true },
91	          lines: {
92	            type: 'array',
93	            required: true,
94	            items: {
95	              type: 'object',
96	              additionalProperties: false,
97	              properties: {
98	                number: { type: 'integer', required: true },
99	                text: { type: 'string', required: true },
100	              },
101	            },
102	          },
103	          totalLines: { type: 'integer', required: true },
104	        },
105	      },
106	      render: (args, value) => {
107	        const input = parseReadArgs(args, caps.limit)
108	        const endLine = value.lines.at(-1)?.number ?? Math.max(0, value.offset - 1)
109	        const truncatedByBytes = value.lines.length < input.limit && endLine < value.totalLines
110	        return [{
111	          type: 'text',
112	          text: formatReadOutput(value.path, {
113	            offset: value.offset,
114	            lines: value.lines,
115	            totalLines: value.totalLines,
116	            ...truncatedByBytes ? { truncatedByBytes: true } : {},
117	          }),
118	        }]
119	      },
120	      // Project the structured window into persisted `meta` so a UI's read card
121	      // survives replay: the raw canonical output object is not on the wire, only
122	      // the model-facing text, from which the line/lang data cannot be recovered.
123	      presentationMeta: (_args, value) => {
124	        const lang = langFromPath(value.path)
125	        return {
126	          path: value.path,
127	          offset: value.offset,
128	          lines: value.lines.map(({ number, text }) => ({ number, text })),
129	          totalLines: value.totalLines,
130	          ...lang === undefined ? {} : { lang },
131	        }
132	      },
133	    },
134	    // Observation races fail closed because guarded mutations re-check the version in-lock.
135	    isConcurrencySafe: () => true,
136	    async execute(args, exec) {
137	      const input = parseReadArgs(args, caps.limit)
138	      // One stat: absence observation OR type check + size routing + present version.
139	      // A concurrent write can only make a later guarded mutation fail stale and require reread.
140	      const { target, info } = await resolveRegularReadTarget(ctx, exec, input.filePath)
141	
142	      // Stream when the file is large OR size is unknown, so a size-less backend
143	      // never buffers an arbitrarily large file.
144	      const chunks = info.size === undefined || info.size >= caps.streamMinSize
145	        ? await ctx.fs.streamText(target, exec.signal)
146	        : [await ctx.fs.readText(target, exec.signal)]
147	      const window = await buildWindow(
148	        chunks,
149	        { offset: input.offset, limit: input.limit, maxLineLength: caps.maxLineLength, maxBytes: caps.maxBytes },
150	        target.displayPath,
151	      )
152	
153	      const outcome = {
154	        path: target.displayPath,
155	        offset: input.offset,
156	        lines: window.lines,
157	        totalLines: window.totalLines,
158	      }
159	      // Record the present observation (a no-op when no policy plugin listens). The
160	      // read already succeeded; an fs/observed listener is contractually a
161	      // synchronous, side-effect-only recorder.
162	      ctx.emit('fs/observed', target, { kind: 'present', version: info.version }, exec)
163	      return outcome
164	    },
165	    // Result-time display: a `read` card carrying the structured line window a
166	    // capable UI renders as a line-numbered, syntax-highlighted view. The
167	    // structured data is narrowed from the persisted `meta` (replay-safe); the
168	    // envelope-stripped model-facing text rides along as `content` so a UI without
169	    // the read capability still shows the file text. A malformed or absent meta,
170	    // or a result whose text is not the read envelope, declines to `undefined`
171	    // (the generic fallback), never throwing on replay of obsolete logged output.
172	    presentResult(_args, result: ToolResult): ReadResultView | undefined {
173	      if (result.isError) return undefined
174	      const meta = readMetaFromMeta(result.meta)
175	      if (meta === undefined) return undefined
176	      const only = result.content.length === 1 ? result.content[0] : undefined
177	      const text = only?.type === 'text' ? only.text : undefined
178	      if (text === undefined) return undefined
179	      // Group 1 always captures (possibly empty) when the envelope matches.
180	      const body = /^<path>[^\n]*<\/path>\n<type>file<\/type>\n<content>\n([\s\S]*)\n<\/content>$/u.exec(text)?.[1]
181	      if (body === undefined) return undefined
182	      return {
183	        card: 'read',
184	        path: meta.path,
185	        offset: meta.offset,
186	        lines: meta.lines,
187	        totalLines: meta.totalLines,
188	        ...meta.lang === undefined ? {} : { lang: meta.lang },
189	        content: [{ type: 'text', text: body }],
190	      }
191	    },
192	    // Pure display: a generic card titled by the file with the read window appended (`Read
193	    // foo.txt (5 - 8)`), `read` kind (icon), and a follow-along location whose line is the
194	    // read's offset (defaulting to 1). The window reflects raw args, so an omitted limit keeps
195	    // the title bare instead of smuggling config into this pure presenter.
196	    presentCall(args): GenericCallView {
197	      const { offset, limit } = args
198	      const window = limit !== undefined && limit > 0
199	        ? ` (${offset ?? 1} - ${(offset ?? 1) + limit - 1})`
200	        : offset !== undefined ? ` (from line ${offset})` : ''
201	      return {
202	        card: 'generic',
203	        title: `Read ${args.file_path}${window}`,
204	        kind: 'read',
205	        locations: [{ path: args.file_path, line: offset ?? 1 }],
206	      }
207	    },
208	  }))
209	}

2	 * Shared path resolution and regular-file validation for model-facing read tools.

4	 */

6	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
7	import { FsError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs'
8	import type { FsInfo, FsTarget } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs'
9	import type { ToolExecution } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
10	import { sessionResolveOptions } from './session-cwd.ts'

12	/**
13	 * Resolve a model-supplied path, observe absence, and require a regular file.
14	 * @param ctx - the plugin context providing filesystem resolution and observation events.
15	 * @param exec - the current tool execution, including session cwd and cancellation.
16	 * @param requestedPath - the raw path supplied to the tool.
17	 * @returns the resolved target and its single stat result.
18	 */
19	export async function resolveRegularReadTarget(
20	  ctx: Context,
21	  exec: ToolExecution,
22	  requestedPath: string,
23	): Promise<{ target: FsTarget; info: FsInfo }> {
24	  const target = await ctx.fs.resolve(requestedPath, sessionResolveOptions(exec, requestedPath))
25	  const info = await ctx.fs.stat(target, exec.signal)
26	  if (info === undefined) {
27	    ctx.emit('fs/observed', target, { kind: 'absent' }, exec)
28	    throw new FsError(`cannot read "${target.displayPath}": not found`, 'FS_NOT_FOUND')
29	  }
30	  if (info.type !== 'file') {
31	    throw new FsError(`cannot read "${target.displayPath}": not a regular file`, 'FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE')
32	  }
33	  return { target, info }
34	}

4	 * environment it runs, authors the completion standard from the environment's

6	 * executes the checks through the shell executor after each turn, records the
7	 * run, and completes the goal only under a certificate. The

49	/** Stable error codes of a refused or broken run. */
50	export type EnvironmentRunErrorCode =
51	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT'
52	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE'
53	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE'

55	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_STANDARD_LOST'

57	/** Error returned by the environment runner boundary. */
58	export class EnvironmentRunError extends HarnessError {
59	  /**
60	   * @param message - human-readable reason.
61	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
62	   */

64	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing

70	/** Deployment choices of the runner, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
71	export interface Config {
72	  /** Isolation the deployment can defend for its check runs; written into every certificate and stamp. */
73	  isolation: CertificateIsolation
74	  /** Implementer turns before the run is reported uncertified; each is followed by one validation. */
75	  maxAttempts?: number

83	
84	/** The runner's choices with every default applied. */
85	export interface ResolvedConfig {
86	  readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation
87	  readonly maxAttempts: number
88	  readonly maxGoalRounds: number | undefined
89	  readonly checkTimeoutMs: number | undefined
90	  readonly evidenceMaxChars: number
91	}
92	
93	/**
94	 * Apply the runner's defaults to a validated config.
95	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
96	 * @returns the resolved choices: one attempt and 2000 evidence characters unless configured.
97	 */
98	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
99	  return {
100	    isolation: config.isolation,
101	    maxAttempts: config.maxAttempts ?? 1,
102	    maxGoalRounds: config.maxGoalRounds,
103	    checkTimeoutMs: config.checkTimeoutMs,
104	    evidenceMaxChars: config.evidenceMaxChars ?? 2000,
105	  }
106	}

108	/** Directory test that treats a missing or unreadable path as no directory. */
109	async function isDirectory(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
110	  try {
111	    return (await stat(path)).isDirectory()
112	  } catch {
113	    // stat rejects for a missing or unreadable path; both mean the caller named no usable directory.
114	    return false
115	  }
116	}
117	
118	/** SHA-256 over every regular file under a directory: relative POSIX path, then bytes, in sorted order. */
119	async function hashDirectory(root: string): Promise<string> {
120	  const entries = await readdir(root, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
121	  const files = entries.filter(entry => entry.isFile()).map(entry => join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)).sort()
122	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
123	  for (const file of files) {
124	    hash.update(relative(root, file).split(sep).join('/')).update('\0').update(await readFile(file)).update('\0')
125	  }
126	  return hash.digest('hex')
127	}
128	
129	/**
130	 * Reject a workspace or fixture that is not an existing absolute directory,
131	 * then overlay the fixture and return its digest.
132	 * @returns the fixture digest, or `undefined` for a task without a fixture.
133	 */
134	async function prepareWorkspace(workspace: string, fixture: string | undefined): Promise<string | undefined> {
135	  if (!isAbsolute(workspace) || !await isDirectory(workspace)) {
136	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`workspace "${workspace}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE')
137	  }
138	  if (fixture === undefined) return undefined
139	  if (!isAbsolute(fixture) || !await isDirectory(fixture)) {
140	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`fixture "${fixture}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE')
141	  }
142	  await cp(fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
143	  return hashDirectory(fixture)
144	}
145	
146	/**
147	 * Overlay the fixture again so implementer edits to validator-owned files do
148	 * not reach the checks, then digest the workspace the validation will read.
149	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory.
150	 * @param fixture - the task fixture, absent for a task without one.
151	 * @returns the workspace digest as the validation begins.
152	 */
153	async function restoreFixture(workspace: string, fixture: string | undefined): Promise<string> {
154	  if (fixture !== undefined) await cp(fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
155	  return hashDirectory(workspace)
156	}
157	
158	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
159	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
160	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted
161	}
162	
163	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
164	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
165	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
166	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
167	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
168	  const marker = '\n…'
169	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
170	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
171	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
172	}
173	
174	/** Render one executed check's evidence: the exit fact, then the bounded output tails. */
175	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
176	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
177	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
178	  const lines = [`${exit}${cause}`]
179	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
180	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
181	  return bound(lines.join('\n'), maxChars)
182	}
183	
184	/** One directive per failed run: the count as root cause, the evidence as detail, never the checks themselves. */
185	function describeFailures(failures: readonly CheckResult[], maxChars: number): DirectiveRequest {
186	  return {
187	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
188	    detail: bound(failures.map((failure, index) => `${index + 1}. ${failure.evidence}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
189	  }
190	}
191	
192	/** The validator's follow-up turn after a failed run; the text is pinned by the runner README and its e2e. */
193	function followupText(directive: DirectiveRequest): string {
194	  return `<validation_failed>\n${directive.rootCause}\n${directive.detail}\nContinue working on the task; the validator runs again when you stop.\n</validation_failed>`
195	}
196	
197	/** Sum the usage of every assistant message in a session log. */
198	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
199	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
200	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
201	  ))
202	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
203	  const total: TokenUsage = {
204	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
205	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
206	  }
207	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
208	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
209	      const value = step[key]
210	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
211	    })
212	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
213	  }
214	  return total
215	}

217	/** Environment runner (`ctx.environmentRuns`): one registered environment as one validated session. */
218	export class EnvironmentRunner extends Service {
219	  static inject = ['environments', 'agents', 'agentDefaultModel', 'goals', 'completionStandards', 'shell', 'sessions']
220	
221	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
222	    isolation: z.union(['none', 'process', 'host'] as const).required(),
223	    maxAttempts: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
224	    maxGoalRounds: z.natural().min(1),
225	    checkTimeoutMs: z.natural().min(1),
226	    evidenceMaxChars: z.natural().min(1).default(2000),
227	  })
228	
229	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
230	
231	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
232	    super(ctx, 'environmentRuns')
233	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
234	  }
235	
236	  /**
237	   * Run one environment as one fresh session and validate it.
238	   * @param request - environment id, absolute workspace directory, optional model route, repetition, group, and abort signal.
239	   * @returns the stamp, the attempts, the certificate when one run passed, and the accumulated usage.
240	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} for an unknown environment, an unusable
241	   *   workspace or fixture, an implementer that replaced the goal, or a lost standard.
242	   */
243	  async run(request: EnvironmentRunRequest): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
244	    const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(request.environment)
245	    if (definition === undefined) {
246	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`environment "${request.environment}" is not registered`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT')
247	    }
248	    const fixtureSha256 = await prepareWorkspace(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
249	    const model = request.model ?? this.defaultModel()
250	    const stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp = {
251	      kind: 'environment/run',
252	      version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
253	      environmentId: definition.id,
254	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
255	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
256	      ...environmentContentHashes(definition, fixtureSha256),
257	      repetition: request.repetition ?? 0,
258	      ...request.group === undefined ? {} : { group: request.group },
259	      model,
260	      isolation: this.resolved.isolation,
261	    }
262	    const handle = await this.ctx.agents.create({
263	      sessionId: SessionId(`environment-${randomUUID()}`),
264	      meta: { cwd: request.workspace },
265	      agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
266	      ...request.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: request.signal },
267	      setup: (agentCtx) => {
268	        installModelSelection(agentCtx, { current: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model }, assembled: undefined })
269	      },
270	    })
271	    try {
272	      return await this.drive(handle.agent, definition, stamp, request)
273	    } finally {
274	      await handle.dispose()
275	    }
276	  }
277	
278	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
279	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
280	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
281	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
282	  }
283	
284	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
285	  private async drive(
286	    agent: Agent,
287	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
288	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
289	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
290	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
291	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
292	    await agent.whenIdle()
293	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
294	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {
295	      objective: definition.task.prompt,
296	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
297	    })
298	    goals.disarm(agent)
299	    completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
300	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
301	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
302	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
303	    try {
304	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
305	        agent.followup(createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: prompt }], source: { kind: 'user' } }))
306	        await agent.whenIdle()
307	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
308	        const treeHash = await restoreFixture(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
309	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request)
310	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
311	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
312	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
313	          executor: 'runner',
314	          treeHash,
315	        })
316	        if (outcome.certified) {
317	          certificate = outcome.certificate
318	          const current = goals.get(agent)
319	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
320	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')
321	          }
322	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
323	          break
324	        }
325	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)
326	        completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, directive)
327	        prompt = followupText(directive)
328	      }
329	    } finally {
330	      await sessions.flush(agent.session)
331	    }
332	    const usage = totalUsage(agent.session.events)
333	    return {
334	      environment: definition.id,
335	      sessionId: agent.id,
336	      stamp,
337	      attempts,
338	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
339	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
340	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
341	    }
342	  }
343	
344	  /** The standard the run measures; the implementer cannot mutate it, so another goal's standard or none is an anomaly. */
345	  private currentStandard(agent: Agent, goalId: GoalId): StandardView {
346	    const standard = this.ctx.completionStandards.get(agent)
347	    if (standard === undefined || standard.goalId !== goalId) {
348	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the standard for goal "${goalId}" is no longer current`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_STANDARD_LOST')
349	    }
350	    return standard
351	  }
352	
353	  /** Run every active check in order through the shell executor rooted at the workspace. */
354	  private async execute(checks: readonly StandardCheck[], request: EnvironmentRunRequest): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
355	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
356	    for (const check of checks) {
357	      const spec = this.ctx.shell.resolve({
358	        command: check.run,
359	        workdir: request.workspace,
360	        timeoutMs: this.resolved.checkTimeoutMs,
361	        signal: request.signal,
362	      })
363	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(spec)
364	      results.push({
365	        checkId: check.id,
366	        status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
367	        evidence: evidenceOf(result, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
368	      })
369	    }
370	    return results
371	  }
372	}
373	
374	export default EnvironmentRunner
